A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IA2 study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, accuracy and calibration measurements, activation analyses, and statistical comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds soft-label distillation comparisons and LoRA sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The activation-collection procedure, alignment objective, and sequential IA2→SFT pipeline remain unchanged. Joint IA2+SFT training already appears in v1; the new LoRA sweeps test parameter choices without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same classification, remapped multiple-choice, mathematics, and open-ended QA coverage, including the same distribution-shift evaluations. V2's additions use existing datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated soft-label knowledge-distillation baseline using ICL teacher responses on Llama models: GSM8K at N=4 and SST2 at N=8 (Table 4). V1 includes hard-response SFT and IA2 variants but lacks this comparator.

E3.justification: The new Appendix B experiments compare LoRA ranks 8 and 16 and QK, QKV, and QKO target modules on selected existing tasks. The previously reported splits, metrics, model configurations, and generation limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted LoRA sensitivity tests asking whether the advantage depends on rank or target modules (Appendix B, Table 7). Section 6 also adds a focused analysis of the math-performance gap to ICL across shot counts (Table 5). Existing activation, subspace, and overfitting analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations and use the same paired t-tests. V1 Table 5 becomes v2 Table 8 with identical statistics. The new experiments follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 17 original tables retain their numerical contents after matching. V2 adds soft-label baseline results, including 36.1% GSM8K and 55.9% SST2 accuracy (Table 4), and LoRA ablation results (Table 7). Table 5 reuses existing N=2/4 math scores and newly tabulates N=8 scores and performance gaps.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, activation-similarity definitions, and the subspace-overlap calculation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that ICL and SFT differ internally and that IA2 priming improves SFT accuracy and calibration. The added intention to study RL-tuned models is future work, not a new demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: V2 proposes Qwen's STEM mid-training as a possible explanation for its strong math ICL performance and discusses the shrinking gap with more shots. It also interprets the new LoRA ablations and soft-label comparison. The mid-training explanation is explicitly speculative.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses a maximum of 50 training epochs and specifies configurations for the added LoRA ablations. The PDFs do not establish that the epoch limit changed operationally. Answer-parsing details are relocated from Appendix A, and code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hinton et al. (2015) for knowledge distillation, Jiang et al. (2025) for DART, and Wei et al. (2022) for chain-of-thought prompting. These additions extend the context locally without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, moves answer-parsing explanations into Section 5 and subspace-overlap details into Section 5.2, and expands Sections 6 and Appendix B. The overall narrative and section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4, 5, and 7 for distillation, math-performance gaps, and LoRA ablations. Existing tables and figures are repositioned and tables renumbered, while their display styles and the six figures' substantive contents remain stable.

improvement.justification: The soft-label comparator and LoRA ablations address missing controls in v1, making the benefits and limits of activation alignment easier to assess. The improvement is bounded by the targeted experimental scope; the proposed explanation of Qwen's math advantage remains untested. These additions strengthen the evidence without resolving a major paper-wide deficiency.
